utterances.text: In that same paragraph, you say that the Kursumli Medresa was badly damaged and could no longer be used. It was hit by several shells. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A couple of sentences earlier you say that the Beg mosque was hit about a hundred times. Did you say that?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This doesn't seem to be plausible to me. If several shells make a building unusable and then you say that the mosque was hit a hundred times, what would have been left of it if it had really been hit 100 times?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN
utterances.text: The Kursumli Medresa, as opposed to the Beg mosque, is a much lighter building with steel roofing and was built quite differently. It's a low building with cupolas, with domes, and as soon as those roofs fell through, it was destroyed with a couple of shells, whereas the Begove mosque is a big building, built I don't know exactly when, it's an old building which has much stronger walls. I saw that for myself because I conducted an inquest in the yard of the mosque. When a mortar shell hits the wall of the Begove mosque, it doesn't cause damage at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it was hit a hundred times yet it wasn't badly damaged?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN
utterances.text: It couldn't be used. The roof was totally destroyed. It had to be supported from the inside. There was red foil on top so that it would -- the rain wouldn't soak through, and people would enter for service like that. But it was still standing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. In your statement of 1996, in paragraphs 2 to 5 about the sniping of a tram, you say that it was established that it was hit from the fourth skyscraper in Grbavica. That's what you say, that you established that.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN
utterances.text: I'm sorry, which paragraph did you say?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The fourth paragraph, page 2. From paragraphs 2 to 5 you talk about the firing at trams from the fourth skyscraper in Grbavica.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN
utterances.text: Among others, from that skyscraper.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking you the following, because you say there that you established in that paragraph, and I'm quoting, you're saying: "Unfortunately, the fire caused certain damage to the tram which prevented us from moving the tram back to its original position when determining the origin, the source of fire." So you were unable to establish that because you were unable to turn the tram back. "So determining the elevation and direction of fire and interviewing the driver of the tram, we were able to establish that the origin of the fire was the fourth skyscraper." So in your own words you were unable to analyse the situation properly but you relied on the statement of the driver.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN
utterances.text: Among others the driver. The entry angle, I don't know whether you know how this is established --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but you say that because of the damage you were not able to push the tram back to establish that angle. So you are guessing, yet you say that you did establish it.

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN
utterances.text: I said that we established it in this way. The angle of fire when the tram was coming by in that area. It was not difficult for us to measure the height of the shell and then check it out, though this is the job of a criminal technician and a ballistics expert. My job is just to carry out the investigation, to take note of all the details, and others analyse it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: This must be your last question, Mr. Milosevic, today.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In that same paragraph you said, and I quote you: "Of a total of eight rounds, four passed through the tram, causing entry and exit holes." So you established that four had hit the tram. How did you know that there were eight? It's clear for the four but how can you know how many rounds missed?

utterances.speaker: MIRSAD KUCANIN
utterances.text: I think this is the translation that is rather strange. I was looking at my own notes. Four rounds went through the metal of the tram, and the others went through the glass. These four entered through the metal shell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. So this is an error in the translation. So let's leave that as it is for now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. We will adjourn now. Mr. Milosevic, you will have 20 minutes left tomorrow to continue your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Before just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Just a moment. Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Just before we adjourn, might I indicate that tomorrow the Prosecution proposes to call B-1524 following the testimony of Mr. Franken. We had intended to -- I think he was scheduled for an earlier time but did not testify on that occasion because we ran out of time. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. Yes, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In this list I received from the side opposite, I saw that this witness is testifying for two hours so I thought I had a little more time. You're just telling me that I have another 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: It's a normal 92 bis witness. I think the Prosecution were miscalculating there. Is there any particular reason -- what is there in particular that you want to ask this witness which is going to take up more time? Anything in particular?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I must look through my notes, but I had planned the time according to the information I had received. That's what I'm talking about. I'm asking him questions about his statements and in connection with his testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We will give you half an hour tomorrow in case you've been misled. Mr. Kucanin, that concludes the evidence for today. I must warn you, as we warn all witnesses, please, not to speak to anybody about their evidence until it's over, and that does include the members of the Prosecution team. Could you be back, please, at 9.00 tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 13th day of November, 2003, at 9.00 a.m. 22 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.55 p.m.,
